text:
Alex: Heads up — p99 for /v1/generate jumped after yesterday's routing tweak. Dashboard p99 went from ~420ms to ~1.2s around 18:40 UTC.
Priya: saw that too, mostly in eu-west. p50/p95 stable.
Tom: could be queueing/backpressure in gateway or a dependency spike. Any config changes to dispatch queues?
Alex: we changed route weights and increased max inflight on the routing policy for tier=free to allow more burst.
Maria: that could increase head-of-line blocking for some clients if batching changed. Do we have the per-endpoint queue depth heatmap?
Alex: grabbing logs. quick grep: `grep \"/v1/generate\" gateway.log | tail -n 50` shows several `dispatch_wait=480ms` entries and a few `backend_time=600-900ms`.
Priya: interesting — dispatch_wait appears frequently in concerned timeframe. That suggests gateway is delaying requests before sending to serving pool.
Tom: is this correlated with any quota enforcement or rate-limiter token refill? If token buckets were throttling, we might see queued bursts.
Alex: quota config unchanged. But routing change also bumped burst capacity on pooled routes which may have changed batching shapes.
Maria: can you paste a tiny snippet of the log lines (sanitized)?
Alex: sure:
```
2026-03-20T18:39:21Z INFO request id=abc123 path=/v1/generate dispatch_wait=472ms backend_time=680ms total=1156ms
2026-03-20T18:39:22Z INFO request id=abc124 path=/v1/generate dispatch_wait=50ms backend_time=430ms total=480ms
```
Priya: that first line matches the p99 spike. Dispatch wait is the big delta. Backend time also high on that one. Could be model variant fallback?
Tom: check model variant routing — if a request falls back from fast-quantized to higher-latency variant, backend_time goes up. But dispatch_wait still primary.
Maria: dashboard sampling could hide this if we only sample traces for p50/p95. We need to verify sampling strategy for percentiles. Are percentiles calculated from raw samples or sampled traces?
Priya: console uses rollup counts from tdigest aggregation from stream; sampling is only for traces, not for raw latency time-series. So the metric should be accurate.
Alex: I ran an ad-hoc query against raw logs for that minute and found ~120 requests; ~6 had dispatch_wait > 300ms. That explains p99 shift.
Tom: root causes: increased queueing at gateway OR temporary spike from a heavy client. Can we annotate dashboard with routing-change and compare caller tags?
Maria: yes — add annotation and filter by `caller:mobile-web`. If it's a single client causing head-of-line, we might throttle at client-level or adjust queue fairness.
Priya: also check if KV cache hit rates dropped — more cold cache could push backend_time up.
Alex: KV cache hit% stayed ~92% — not the issue.
Tom: plan: 1) annotate dashboard (Alex), 2) correlate by caller & route (Priya), 3) revert routing weight tweak in staging and simulate (Maria), 4) open postmortem if it's systemic (Tom).
Alex: created ticket INF-6321 and annotated dashboard with message: "routing policy change: increased burst capacity for tier=free".
deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-20 18:38 UTC: routing-policy-service v2.14.0 -> v2.15.0 (actor: priya) :white_check_mark:
Priya: thanks — I'll run quick query to split p99 by caller and model-variant.
Alex: thanks. If it's a client-level burst, short-term mitigation: reduce max inflight for that route or enable per-caller concurrency caps.
Maria: agree. For longer-term UX we should expose per-route queue depth and dispatch_wait percentile in the console — p50/p95/p99 for `dispatch_wait` separate from `backend_time` so customers can quickly see whether gateway queuing or backend is the problem.
Tom: +1. Also add an alert rule for sustained p99 dispatch_wait > 300ms for 5m.
Priya: I'll add a follow-up to the routing-policy RFC to mention fairness and head-of-line risk when bumping burst capacity.
Alex: ok closing this thread for now — let's sync in the rollout review tomorrow + include demo of the per-route dispatch_wait panel. :thumbsup:
Maria: thanks all.
Tom: leaving notes in INF-6321 about suggested mitigations.
Priya: update: split-by-caller shows 85% of the high dispatch_wait came from a single mobile client id. Opening support case to ask them to backoff.
